descriptor: Transport Technology / Telematics SaaS · reported in NZD

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
charts.annotation: FY2026 and H1 FY2026 net income includes a NZ$134.7m non-cash goodwill/other-asset impairment on the North American CGU -- see the impairment chart below, not a data error.

charts.title: Normalised EBIT vs Reported Operating Income
charts.annotation: Normalised EBIT is EROAD's own non-GAAP measure (used throughout its results presentations); it strips one-offs including the FY2026 impairment that reported operating income absorbs in full.

charts.title: Goodwill & Other-Asset Impairment
charts.annotation: NZ$134.7m North American CGU impairment recognised in H1 FY2026 and carried through FY2026 -- the single largest driver of the FY2026 net loss.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal. Net income in FY2026/H1 FY2026 is depressed by a NZ$134.7m non-cash impairment that does not flow through cash flow -- see the impairment chart.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For EROAD Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For EROAD Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For EROAD Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For EROAD Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For EROAD Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For EROAD Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For EROAD Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For EROAD Limited: FY2026 net income (-$82.5m) and H1 FY2026 (-$145.5m) both absorb a NZ$134.7m non-cash goodwill/other-asset impairment on the North American CGU. See the dedicated impairment chart and the Normalised EBIT chart below before reading this as an operating collapse.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs, impairments)

normalisedEbit.title: Normalised EBIT
normalisedEbit.content:
Normalised EBIT is EROAD's own non-GAAP operating profit measure, disclosed alongside statutory results and used throughout its investor presentations. It excludes significant one-off items -- most importantly the FY2026 North American goodwill/other-asset impairment -- that reported operating income includes in full.

For EROAD Limited: Normalised EBIT fell from $9.9m (FY2025) to $2.9m (FY2026) -- a genuine deterioration in the underlying business, but a far smaller one than the statutory operating income line suggests once the impairment is stripped out.

What to watch:

  • Whether Normalised EBIT is itself trending toward or away from statutory operating income (a widening gap means more items are being normalised away)
  • Management's own definition of Normalised EBIT can change between periods -- check the reconciliation in the results presentation

impairment.title: Goodwill and other-asset impairment
impairment.content:
A non-cash write-down of goodwill or other assets when their carrying value exceeds recoverable value, taken through the income statement.

For EROAD Limited: a NZ$134.7m impairment against the North American cash-generating unit (CGU) was recognised in H1 FY2026 and stands for the full FY2026 year -- it is the primary reason reported net income swung from +$1.4m (FY2025) to -$82.5m (FY2026), and the FY2026 EPS/margin lines should be read alongside it, not independently.

What to watch:

  • Whether the North American business subsequently returns to the growth assumed when that goodwill was first recognised
  • Further impairments would signal the carrying value is still too high
  • Impairments are non-cash: they do not by themselves affect free cash flow or covenant cash balances

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For EROAD Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For EROAD Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
